quests.instruction: Zoya's room is a mess by Friday every week, and she spends Saturday morning tidying. What change would help most?
quests.correctAnswer: Put Things Away as She Uses Them 🧸
options: Stop Playing With Her Toys at All 🚫
Tidy Only Once Every Month or So 📅
Put Things Away as She Uses Them 🧸
quests.hint: Work out how a mess builds up.
quests.explanation: Putting things away right after using them stops the mess from building up, so there is far less to do later. Tidying once a month would make it worse.
quests.funFact: Small, regular tidy-ups are easier to keep up than one big clear-out.

quests.instruction: Hari starts his homework after dinner, but he is sleepy and makes mistakes. What should he change?
quests.correctAnswer: Start Earlier, Before He Gets Tired ⏰
options: Start Earlier, Before He Gets Tired ⏰
Skip Dinner to Save Time Tonight 🍽️
Do It While Lying Down in Bed 🛏️
quests.hint: Ask yourself when his energy is best.
quests.explanation: Starting earlier means he works while he is fresh. Skipping dinner or working in bed would not help.
quests.funFact: Energy and alertness change during the day, and many people feel a dip in the early afternoon.

quests.instruction: Ila keeps forgetting to water her plant. Which change would help her remember?
quests.correctAnswer: Do It Straight After Breakfast 🪴
options: Water It Whenever She Remembers 🤷
Do It Straight After Breakfast 🪴
Wait Until the Leaves Droop Badly 🍂
quests.hint: Think about linking it to something she already does each day.
quests.explanation: Tying a new job to an everyday habit gives her a clear reminder. Waiting until she remembers or until the leaves droop leaves it to chance.
quests.funFact: Linking a new habit to an existing one is a technique that psychologists call habit stacking.

quests.instruction: Aman forgets his lunch box at home. Which reaction is the least helpful?
quests.correctAnswer: Sulking All Day and Eating Nothing 😠
options: Asking a Friend to Share Lunch 🤝
Sulking All Day and Eating Nothing 😠
Telling His Teacher What Happened 🙋
quests.hint: Ask yourself which reactions actually solve the problem.
quests.explanation: Sulking does not solve anything and leaves him hungry. Telling the teacher or asking a friend to share gets him a meal.
quests.funFact: A school office or canteen can often help a child who forgets lunch, for example by calling home.

quests.instruction: Priya gets a low mark on a test. Which response would help her least?
quests.correctAnswer: Deciding She Is Bad at It and Giving Up 🏳️
options: Deciding She Is Bad at It and Giving Up 🏳️
Asking the Teacher How She Can Improve 🙋
Practising the Hard Questions Once More 📝
quests.hint: Work out which reaction closes the door on getting better.
quests.explanation: Giving up stops any improvement. Asking for feedback and practising are what help people get better.
quests.funFact: Teachers often encourage children to add the word 'yet', as in 'I can't do this yet', to remind them that skills grow with practice.

quests.instruction: Leo loses his favourite pen. Which reaction would make things worse?
quests.correctAnswer: Taking Someone Else's Pen Without Asking 🖊️
options: Asking at the Lost Property Box in School 🧑
Retracing His Steps Around School 🔍
Taking Someone Else's Pen Without Asking 🖊️
quests.hint: Work out which reaction creates a new problem.
quests.explanation: Taking a pen without asking creates a new problem for someone else. Looking back over where he has been and checking lost property can find his own.
quests.funFact: Writing your name on your belongings makes it easier for them to find their way back to you.

quests.instruction: Which choice is a mistake when crossing the road?
quests.correctAnswer: Looking at a Screen While Crossing 📱
options: Waiting for the Signal to Turn Green 🚦
Looking at a Screen While Crossing 📱
Holding a Grown-up's Hand Firmly 🤝
quests.hint: Decide what your eyes and ears should be doing.
quests.explanation: Looking at a screen takes attention off the traffic, so a vehicle can be missed. Waiting for the signal and holding a hand are safe habits.
quests.funFact: Some cities have even introduced rules against using phones while crossing the road.

quests.instruction: Which is a mistake when taking a plug out of a socket?
quests.correctAnswer: Pulling It Out by the Wire 🔌
options: Gripping the Plug Itself 🤲
Pulling It Out by the Wire 🔌
Asking a Grown-up to Switch Off 🧑
quests.hint: Think about what could be damaged if you yank the cable.
quests.explanation: Pulling on the wire can loosen or expose the wires inside, which is dangerous. Holding the plug itself is the right way.
quests.funFact: Damaged cables are a common cause of electrical accidents at home.

quests.instruction: Which habit is a mistake on a playground swing?
quests.correctAnswer: Standing Up on the Swing ⚠️
options: Sitting and Holding the Chains ⛓️
Waiting Until It Stops to Get Off 🛑
Standing Up on the Swing ⚠️
quests.hint: Remember what could happen if you lose your balance.
quests.explanation: Standing on a swing makes a fall from a height more likely. Sitting, holding on and waiting for it to stop keep you safe.
quests.funFact: A swing moves like a pendulum, swinging back and forth in a steady rhythm.

quests.instruction: Which idea about routines is NOT true?
quests.correctAnswer: A Routine Can Never Be Changed 🔒
options: A Routine Can Help Us Remember Things 🧠
A Routine Can Bend on Special Days 🎉
A Routine Can Never Be Changed 🔒
quests.hint: Consider whether routines can adapt.
quests.explanation: Routines can be adjusted when life changes, such as on holidays or when plans shift. Their purpose is to help us, not to trap us.
quests.funFact: Routines are usually revised when something big changes, such as a new school or a new baby.

quests.instruction: Which idea about sleep is mistaken?
quests.correctAnswer: Sleeping Less Gives You More Energy ⚡
options: Enough Sleep Helps You Focus Well 🧠
Sleeping Less Gives You More Energy ⚡
Tired Bodies Need Rest and Sleep 🛌
quests.hint: Decide how you feel after a short night.
quests.explanation: Too little sleep leaves people tired and less able to concentrate. Enough sleep helps the body and brain work well.
quests.funFact: Growth hormone is released during sleep, which is one reason children need plenty of it.

quests.instruction: Which belief about tidying up is wrong?
quests.correctAnswer: Mess Only Matters to Other People 🙈
options: Mess Only Matters to Other People 🙈
A Tidy Space Is Easier to Use 🗂️
Putting Things Back Saves Searching Time ⏳
quests.hint: Consider who is affected by a messy space.
quests.explanation: Mess affects the person who lives in the space too, because things are hard to find and easy to trip over. Tidying helps everyone.
quests.funFact: A clear desk gives the eyes fewer things to look at, which helps people start work.

quests.instruction: Meera gets a tummy ache after eating her lunch in three minutes. What change would help next time?
quests.correctAnswer: Eat Slowly and Chew Well 🍽️
options: Swallow Without Chewing 😬
Eat Even Faster 🏃
Eat Slowly and Chew Well 🍽️
quests.hint: Decide what the mouth and the stomach each have to do.
quests.explanation: Chewing breaks food into small pieces, which makes it easier to digest. Eating slowly gives the body time to feel full.
quests.funFact: It can take the brain about twenty minutes to register that the stomach is full.

quests.instruction: Anu gets a blister after wearing new shoes all day for the first time. What change would help?
quests.correctAnswer: Wear Them for Short Spells at First 👟
options: Wear Them for Even Longer Stretches 🕒
Walk Much Faster in Them Today 🏃
Wear Them for Short Spells at First 👟
quests.hint: Think about how shoes soften and feet adjust.
quests.explanation: New shoes are stiff and rub, so short spells let the shoes soften and the skin get used to them.
quests.funFact: Leather shoes soften with wear as the material flexes and stretches.

quests.instruction: Mina's eyes sting after swimming in the pool. What change would help?
quests.correctAnswer: Wear Swimming Goggles 🥽
options: Wear Swimming Goggles 🥽
Keep Her Eyes Wide Open Underwater 👀
Swim Even Faster 🏊
quests.hint: Remember what is in pool water.
quests.explanation: Pool water often contains chlorine, which can irritate eyes. Goggles keep it out.
quests.funFact: Chlorine is added to pool water to kill germs, but it can sting the eyes.

quests.instruction: A pet fish becomes ill after being given a handful of food every hour. What was the mistake?
quests.correctAnswer: Giving It Far Too Much Food 🍽️
options: Keeping the Fish Tank Clean 🧼
Giving It Far Too Much Food 🍽️
Talking to It Far Too Much 🗣️
quests.hint: Remember how much a tiny fish can eat.
quests.explanation: Fish need only small amounts. Extra food goes uneaten, rots and dirties the water.
quests.funFact: Fish food is usually given in a pinch small enough for the fish to finish in a couple of minutes.

quests.instruction: The leaves on Ira's plant turn yellow and the soil is soggy. What was the mistake?
quests.correctAnswer: Watering It Too Often 💦
options: Keeping It Near a Window 🪟
Talking to It Gently 🗣️
Watering It Too Often 💦
quests.hint: Think about what soggy soil does to roots.
quests.explanation: Roots need air as well as water, so constantly soggy soil can rot them. Light from a window is good for a plant.
quests.funFact: Most plant pots have a hole in the bottom so that extra water can drain away.

quests.instruction: A dog is tied up in the hot sun all afternoon with no water. What is the mistake?
quests.correctAnswer: No Shade or Water on a Hot Day 🐕
options: Giving It a Bone 🦴
Walking It in the Cool Morning 🌅
No Shade or Water on a Hot Day 🐕
quests.hint: Think about how hot weather affects animals.
quests.explanation: Dogs can overheat quickly, so they need shade and fresh water on hot days.
quests.funFact: Dogs cool down mainly by panting, because they sweat very little.

quests.instruction: Kabir copies whole sentences from a website into his project. What should he do instead?
quests.correctAnswer: Write It in His Own Words ✍️
options: Write It in His Own Words ✍️
Copy Even More 📋
Hand It In Without Reading It 🙈
quests.hint: The key is showing what he really understands.
quests.explanation: Using his own words shows he understands the topic and gives credit where it is due. Copying passes off someone else's work as his own.
quests.funFact: Copying someone else's writing without saying so is called plagiarism, and it can affect marks.

quests.instruction: Dev's teacher adds up his test marks wrongly and gives him five extra. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell the Teacher About the Mistake 🙋
options: Keep Quiet and Enjoy the Extra Mark 🤫
Tell the Teacher About the Mistake 🙋
Change an Answer to Match the Mark 🖊️
quests.hint: Consider being fair and honest.
quests.explanation: Reporting the error is the fair thing to do, because the extra marks were not earned. Staying silent or altering an answer to hide it would be dishonest.
quests.funFact: Teachers add up marks by hand and sometimes make small mistakes, so checking helps.

quests.instruction: Zoya is given a school tablet for a task but plays games on it during the lesson. What should she do instead?
quests.correctAnswer: Use It Only for the Task 📚
options: Use It Only for the Task 📚
Lend It to a Friend to Play 🤝
Play Quietly So Nobody Notices 🎮
quests.hint: Remember why the tablet was handed out.
quests.explanation: The tablet is there for the lesson, so using it for the task respects the teacher's time and shared equipment.
quests.funFact: School tablets often have filters and rules so that they are used for learning.

quests.instruction: At the park, Dev leaves his bag on a bench while he plays, and it goes missing. What change would help?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep Bags Where He Can See Them 🎒
options: Hide It in the Bushes by the Path 🌿
Leave It Open Instead of Closed 🔓
Keep Bags Where He Can See Them 🎒
quests.hint: Work out how to keep an eye on your things.
quests.explanation: Keeping bags in view means he notices if anyone touches them. Leaving them open or hidden makes loss more likely.
quests.funFact: Notices in public places often remind visitors to keep their belongings with them.

quests.instruction: Anu finds red berries on a bush and wants to taste them. What is the mistake?
quests.correctAnswer: Eating Berries She Does Not Know 🍒
options: Eating Berries She Does Not Know 🍒
Washing Her Hands Afterwards 💧
Asking a Grown-up What They Are 🧑
quests.hint: Remember who knows which plants are safe.
quests.explanation: Some wild berries are poisonous, and even a few can make a child very ill, so she should only eat food a grown-up says is safe.
quests.funFact: Some poisonous berries look very like safe ones, so only a grown-up should decide what can be eaten.

quests.instruction: Zoya goes near a deep pond to look at the frogs without telling anyone. What is the mistake?
quests.correctAnswer: Going Near Water Without a Grown-up 🌊
options: Flying a Kite with a Good Friend 🪁
Going Near Water Without a Grown-up 🌊
Playing on the Open Grass Nearby 🏞️
quests.hint: Think about who should know where you are around water.
quests.explanation: Deep water can be dangerous even for a good swimmer, so a grown-up needs to know where the children are and be watching them.
quests.funFact: Drowning can happen quickly and quietly, which is why adult supervision near water matters.

quests.instruction: Aman has football on Monday, music on Tuesday, swimming on Wednesday, art on Thursday and chess on Friday. He is exhausted. What is the problem?
quests.correctAnswer: Too Many Activities and No Rest Days 📅
options: Too Many Activities and No Rest Days 📅
Too Much Sleep Every Single Night 🛌
Too Much Free Time Every Day ⏳
quests.hint: Work out when he gets to rest.
quests.explanation: A packed week leaves no time to rest, so he is tired. Free time and sleep are what he needs more of.
quests.funFact: Children need free play and rest as well as organised activities.

quests.instruction: Dev does homework for three hours without a break, and he gets restless and makes mistakes. What would help?
quests.correctAnswer: Short Breaks Between Tasks 🍎
options: Longer Tasks Without Stopping 📚
Short Breaks Between Tasks 🍎
No Water or Food Until Done 🚫
quests.hint: Consider how concentration changes over time.
quests.explanation: Short breaks let the mind recover, so he can work more carefully. Longer stretches and going without food or water make it worse.
quests.funFact: Attention tends to fade after a while, which is why teachers change activities during a lesson.

quests.instruction: Priya plays video games all weekend and has no time for rest, chores or family. What would give her a better balance?
quests.correctAnswer: Plan Time for Play, Rest and Family ⚖️
options: Do Nothing but Chores for the Whole Weekend 🧹
Plan Time for Play, Rest and Family ⚖️
Play Games Even More Often Instead 🎮
quests.hint: Consider including everything that matters.
quests.explanation: A balanced plan makes room for play, rest and family. All play or all chores leaves something out.
quests.funFact: Planning a weekend, even roughly, helps people fit in what matters to them.

quests.instruction: Rita's evening plan is dinner at 9:45 and bed at 10:00. What is the weakest part?
quests.correctAnswer: Eating So Close to Bedtime 🍛
options: Going to Bed at 10:00 🛏️
Having Dinner with Her Family 🍽️
Eating So Close to Bedtime 🍛
quests.hint: Consider how the body feels when it is full and lying down.
quests.explanation: A big meal right before lying down can be uncomfortable and make sleep harder. Eating earlier gives the body time to digest.
quests.funFact: Digestion starts straight away but takes several hours to finish.

quests.instruction: You realise halfway through a routine that you forgot a step. What is the best repair?
quests.correctAnswer: Go Back, Do the Step and Carry On 🔁
options: Go Back, Do the Step and Carry On 🔁
Pretend the Missed Step Does Not Matter 🙈
Start the Whole Routine Again 🔄
quests.hint: Think about fixing the gap without wasting time.
quests.explanation: Going back, doing the missing step and carrying on fixes the problem quickly. Ignoring it leaves a gap, and starting over wastes time.
quests.funFact: Checklists help most when people tick them off as they go, not only at the end.

quests.instruction: Which statement shows a mistaken idea about safety rules?
quests.correctAnswer: Safety Rules Are Only for Little Children 🧒
options: Safety Rules Are Only for Little Children 🧒
Adults Follow Safety Rules in Their Daily Lives 🚦
Safety Rules Help Everyone Stay Safe 🦺
quests.hint: Work out whether grown-ups use safety rules.
quests.explanation: Everyone benefits from safety rules, including adults, who wear seat belts, follow signals and use safety equipment.
quests.funFact: Builders wear hard hats, cyclists wear helmets and drivers wear seat belts, because safety matters at every age.
